item.title: Osimhen scores as Galatasaray defeat Lille 4-2 in Champions League thriller
item.description: Nigerian striker Victor Osimhen scored a crucial second-half goal as Galatasaray came from behind to defeat Lille 4-2 in the UEFA Champions League league phase on Wednesday. The Turkish champions recovered from a first-half deficit to secure all three points in an entertaining encounter in France, with six goals scored by both sides. Galatasaray took the lead in the second minute through Yunus Akgün, who converted a rebound from close range after Baris Yilmaz’s cross caused problems in the Lille penalty area. Lille responded five minutes later as Soriba Diaoune equalised in the seventh minute. The forward received a pass from Alexsandro, drove into the box and fired past Galatasaray goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir. The French side continued to threaten and took the lead in the 39th minute when Diaoune scored his second goal of the evening. Assisted by Hakon Arnar Haraldsson, he found space inside the penalty area before sending a first-time effort into the top-right corner. However, Galatasaray restored parity just before the break. Alexey Batrakov rose unmarked to head home Roland Sallai’s delivery in the 44th minute, ensuring both teams went into half-time level at 2-2. The visitors moved ahead again in the 52nd minute when Lille goalkeeper Berke Özer inadvertently turned the ball into his own net. Osimhen extended Galatasaray’s lead nine minutes later, finishing a swift counterattack with a first-time shot from mid-range after receiving a pass from Yilmaz. The goal made it 4-2 and gave Galatasaray a comfortable advantage as they sought to see out the contest. The Nigerian forward had earlier missed a promising opportunity in the 20th minute, while another effort was ruled out for offside in the 69th minute. However, his second-half strike proved decisive in the visitors’ victory. Lille attempted to mount a comeback, bringing on experienced striker Olivier Giroud and making further substitutions in search of goals. Galatasaray, however, remained organised defensively, with Cakir making important saves to frustrate the hosts. Despite late pressure, including a volley from Maurits Kjaergaard that narrowly missed the target, Lille could not find another goal as Galatasaray held on for a 4-2 victory. The result gave the Turkish side a significant boost in their Champions League campaign, while Osimhen’s goal underlined his importance to the team’s attacking threat. item.description: By Adeola Badru The Oyo State Government has activated disease surveillance networks across its 33 local government areas and prepared its Infectious Disease Centre at Olodo as part of emergency measures against a possible Ebola Virus Disease outbreak. The government, however, assured residents that no confirmed case had been recorded in the state. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Oluwaserimi Ajetunmobi, gave the assurance on Wednesday during an interview with journalists in her office, according to a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information, Prince Dotun Oyelade. item.title: Tunji-Ojo mourns Fasoranti, says his wisdom will be missed
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, has said the wisdom and moral clarity of the late Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti will be greatly missed in Nigeria’s political landscape. Fasoranti, an elder statesman and leader of the Yoruba socio-political group, Afenifere, died at the age of 100. In a tribute, Tunji-Ojo said he joined the nation in mourning the late statesman with a heavy heart, describing his death as a significant loss to the country. “In him, Nigeria has lost a true leader and an enduring symbol of our democratic journey,” the minister said. He described Fasoranti’s century-long life as one anchored on selfless service, adding that his legacy stood as a testament to principled leadership. According to Tunji-Ojo, the late elder statesman was a lifelong disciple of the sage, Chief Obafemi Awolowo, and a longstanding leader of Afenifere. He said Fasoranti remained steadfast in his advocacy for justice, true federalism and the dignity of the Yoruba people, while also upholding national unity and democratic values. The minister said the late Afenifere leader’s contributions to the political evolution of Ondo State and Nigeria would remain indelible. He recalled that Fasoranti was recently celebrated in Lagos on attaining the age of 100, describing the occasion as a rare honour that reflected the respect he commanded across generations and political divides. “Only recently, we gathered in Lagos to celebrate him as a centenarian; a rare honour that underscored the depth of respect he commanded across generations and political divides. That celebration of a life well lived now turns to solemn reflection,” he said. Tunji-Ojo extended his condolences to the Fasoranti family, the people of Ondo State, members of Afenifere and all those inspired by the late elder statesman’s life. “May the Almighty grant his soul eternal rest and comfort those he left behind. Adieu, Pa Fasoranti. Your legacy of courage, service, and integrity endures,” the minister said. The post Tunji-Ojo mourns Fasoranti, says his wisdom will be missed appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The Federal Government has identified misinformation and false promises as major drivers of irregular migration, warning that decisions based on misleading information can expose prospective migrants to serious risks and devastating consequences. The warning was contained in a speech by the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS), Kemi Nandap, at a Stakeholder Sensitisation and Engagement Seminar in Abuja on Wednesday. Nandap, who was represented by the Deputy Comptroller-General in charge of Visa and Residency, Dr Franca Usiwoma Nwanneka, said people migrated in pursuit of education, employment, safety and better opportunities, but stressed the need for accurate information to guide their decisions. “Every day people choose to migrate in pursuit of education, employment, safety, and better opportunities. While these aspirations are legitimate, decisions based on misinformation, false promises, or limited awareness of safe and lawful migration pathways can expose individuals to serious risks and devastating consequences,” she said. item.title: Ebola: Edo urges calm, compliance with safety guidelines
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY — The Edo State Government has urged residents to remain calm and comply with public health guidelines following reports of a confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in Nigeria. The Commissioner for Health, Dr Cyril Oshiomhole, made the call on Wednesday during a press briefing on the reported case. Represented by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health, Dr Eighemherio Ikhumosa, Oshiomhole said the state government was monitoring developments in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC). He described the development as a serious public health concern, adding that the ministry was engaging relevant health agencies and partners to strengthen preparedness and response measures. The commissioner advised residents to avoid contact with the blood and other bodily fluids of infected persons, wash their hands regularly with soap and water, and use appropriate alcohol-based hand sanitisers. He also warned against handling the personal belongings of confirmed cases without proper protective measures. Oshiomhole urged anyone who developed symptoms such as fever, weakness, headache or muscle pain, particularly after possible exposure to the virus, to seek immediate medical attention and follow the guidance of health professionals. He further cautioned residents against spreading unverified information that could cause unnecessary panic or undermine public health efforts. The commissioner urged the public to remain vigilant, stay calm and adhere to preventive measures as health authorities monitor the situation. item.title: New literary prize launched for books ‘written with AI’
item.description: Three tech entrepreneurs in France said Wednesday they had launched what they claimed was the first literary prize for books written with artificial intelligence. Named the “Prix Pascal”, it does not have a jury yet or declared prize money, but the initiative is intended to challenge other prizes which are struggling with how to regulate AI and its use by authors. “The prize is open to anyone who writes in French, anywhere in the French-speaking world, with no requirement of nationality or residence, and without a publisher,” said the three entrepreneurs, Philippe Rodriguez, Albin Serviant and Gilles Mentre, in a statement sent to AFP. “Only the work itself matters: an unpublished work of fiction, in French, co-written with an artificial intelligence, that dares to do what has never been read before,” they added. France’s literary world has been roiled since September by allegations that top-selling debut novelist Thelyson Orelien used AI to write his book “It was Either That or Die.” It won the prestigious FNAC prize in early September before Orelien was accused of cheating, which led to him being ejected from the shortlist for the Goncourt, France’s top prize. After weeks of denials, Orelien’s original publisher in Canada, Boreal, said Wednesday that it had “confirmed” that he had used artificial intelligence in the writing process. Initiatives to label books as written by humans are gaining ground in the industry, while the organisers of established literary prizes are rewriting their rules to exclude AI-generated submissions. But the issue poses thorny questions: will authors be allowed to use services such as ChatGPT or Claude for research or writing advice? When does AI-assisted research become AI writing? Submissions for the debut Prix Pascal will be accepted until November 30, with the prize set to be handed out in mid-December, the organisers said. The Country Director of Amnesty International Nigeria, Dr Andrew Mamedu, also said the relationship between the police and citizens remained strained by mistrust, fear and unresolved questions of accountability. He said reports of tear gas being used against citizens commemorating the anniversary had further raised concerns about the police response to peaceful civic expression. “Public relations campaigns alone cannot restore trust. They must earn it through respect for human rights, professionalism, and accountability. The Nigerian Police must understand that citizens are not enemies of the state, and demanding accountability is not a crime,” Mamedu said. He acknowledged measures introduced since the protests, including the disbandment of SARS, revised operational regulations and efforts to improve professionalism, but said allegations of extortion, arbitrary arrests and excessive use of force continued to raise questions about the effectiveness of the reforms. “We must move beyond reforms that exist only on paper. We must measure police reform by citizens’ safety and dignity, not by the number of policies announced,” he said. Mamedu called for a shift from intimidation to community partnership and accountability, noting that difficult working conditions for police officers could not justify violations of citizens’ rights. “A police officer should represent safety, not fear,” he said. On state police, he said decentralisation could improve local intelligence gathering, response times and community engagement if supported by operational independence, transparent recruitment, independent oversight and safeguards against political interference. With the 2027 general elections approaching, Mamedu warned against the use of security personnel to advance partisan interests. He urged the police and other security agencies to protect voters, candidates, journalists, election officials and observers without discrimination. “The police must protect the ballot, not political interests,” he said, calling for credible investigations and appropriate sanctions against security personnel implicated in electoral violence, intimidation or unlawful arrests. The Executive Director of Global Rights, Abiodun Baiyewu, said the demands that triggered the 2020 protests remained largely unmet, citing continuing concerns over alleged extrajudicial killings and arbitrary arrests. She called for the implementation of the ECOWAS Court judgment concerning the Lekki incident and urged the Lagos State Government to publicly account for its response to the recommendations of the judicial panel of inquiry. A human rights lawyer, Idris Faro, however, said the police had made some progress in their relationship with citizens but needed to strengthen internal discipline and sanction erring officers. “The police must continue to weed out the bad eggs and discipline them appropriately,” Faro said. He condemned reports of tear gas being used against peaceful protesters commemorating the anniversary, describing the action as wrong. Faro also urged security agencies to ensure free, fair and credible elections in 2027. Another human rights lawyer, Toluwa Odheke, called for a comprehensive assessment of the country’s policing system, stressing that reforms must go beyond legislation and administrative directives. “The ultimate measure of police reform is not the number of policies announced, units renamed or regulations issued. It is the extent to which the Nigerian people can trust that the law protects them equally,” Odheke said. He warned that state police could reproduce existing abuses if adequate safeguards against political capture and the unaccountable use of force were not established. Similarly, Patrick Onoja, a legal adviser to an educational institution, said the relationship between the police and civilians remained burdened by mistrust and unresolved demands for justice. “A police institution cannot effectively protect a population that is afraid of it. Trust cannot be restored through official statements or commemorative events alone. It must be earned through consistent professional conduct, transparent investigations and accountability,” Onoja said. While acknowledging the difficult conditions under which many police officers operate, Onoja called for improved funding, training, equipment and welfare, alongside stronger internal discipline. The stakeholders maintained that rebuilding public confidence would require measurable improvements in police conduct, transparent investigations of alleged abuses and consistent enforcement of accountability measures. item.title: Dickson hails Kwankwaso at 70, praises leadership
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Seriake Dickson, has congratulated the party’s vice-presidential candidate, Dr Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, on his 70th birthday, describing him as a symbol of visionary leadership and commitment to public service. Dickson, a former governor of Bayelsa State, congratulated Kwankwaso in a goodwill message titled, “70 Salvos for His Excellency, Dr Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso”. He said the former Kano State governor had distinguished himself through years of public service, including his tenure as Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, governor of Kano State and Minister of Defence. “Happy 70th birthday to His Excellency, Dr Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, a remarkable leader whose record of service as Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Governor of Kano State, Minister of Defence, and several other national calls to duty have been marked by visionary leadership, integrity, and commitment to public service,” Dickson said. The NDC leader said Kwankwaso had inspired generations through his belief in Nigeria and his contributions to the country’s development. “You have inspired generations with your belief in Nigeria,” he added. Dickson also said Kwankwaso’s membership of the NDC and partnership with its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, had strengthened hopes for a better Nigeria. “Your membership of our great party, Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, and partnership with His Excellency Peter Obi in the presidential race has drawn more of our people into believing in the possibility of a new Nigeria where everyone is safe, prosperous, and nobody is oppressed,” he said. The former governor wished Kwankwaso good health, peace, joy and renewed strength as he marks the milestone, expressing hope that his years ahead would contribute to building a better future for Nigerians. item.description: Many secondary school students have been hospitalised following a fresh outbreak of methane emission in Ijebu-Ode, Ijebu-Igbo and Ago-Iwoye in Ogun State. The incident occurred on Wednesday morning, affecting students of Anglican Girls Grammar School, including its public and private sections, in Obalende, Ijebu-Ode, as well as Ijebu-Igbo Girls Grammar School. ﻿ Several students were taken to the general hospitals in Ijebu-Ode and Ijebu-Igbo for medical attention, while the odour disrupted academic activities in Ago-Iwoye, prompting some schools to close abruptly and send pupils home. The incident triggered panic among parents, guardians and teachers, some of whom rushed to hospitals to check on the condition of the affected students. However, the General Manager of the Ogun State Environmental Agency (OGEPA), Kehinde Bello, who was on the ground to assess the situation in Ijebu-Ode and that of Ijebu-Igbo, disclosed that the latest occurrence was linked to underground gas emissions previously recorded in Ijebu-Ode since April 2026. Bello stated that the state government was working on the situation with the aim of finding a lasting solution. He said government investigations had indicated that the phenomenon was a natural occurrence associated with geological and tectonic fault lines, rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak. Bello stated that the state government was working on the situation with the aim of finding a lasting solution. He said government investigations had indicated that the phenomenon was a natural occurrence associated with geological and tectonic fault lines, rather than sabotage or a gas pipeline leak. He urged residents to remain calm, assuring them that the affected students were expected to recover after receiving medical attention. “We left the General Hospital earlier, where over 30 students were attended to for common symptoms, according to the doctor, and the findings from the affected students include shortness of breath, stomach disorder, drowsiness, among others. “While some of them needed oxygen to be stabilised, others just needed minor medical attention. As at the time we were leaving the hospital, most of the students had been discharged, but a few are still under monitoring,” he said. “We are presently at Ijebu Igbo Girls Grammar School for assessment and further investigations. We also checked the surrounding area. This odour was not peculiar to the schools alone; those in the environs were also affected. “The Ijebu North LG Chairman also confirmed that he perceived the odour at the LG secretariat too,” Bello added. Meanwhile, residents who were exposed to the odour have been advised to cover their noses and mouths with wet handkerchiefs rather than wear nose masks. The latest incident has renewed concerns over the recurrence of methane emissions in the affected communities, particularly their impact on schools and the safety of children. The Ogun State Government in June attributed the methane emissions recorded in some schools in Ijebu-Ode to natural underground ecological causes, dismissing speculations linking the incidents to spiritual myths or security threats. The Commissioner for Environment, Ola Oresanya, said scientific investigations identified methane and sulphide gases as the major emissions escaping through underground fractures along established fault lines. The affected areas, according to Oresanya, fall within the Ifewara-Zungeru Trans-Atlantic fault line, which stretches from Mojoda through Ijebu-Ode to Osun and Niger states. He also noted that the affected part of Ijebu-Ode was historically forested and largely uninhabited before missionary schools were established there. item.title: Reforms Are Yielding Results, Okpebholo Urges Edo Residents To Back Tinubu’s Re-Election
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has appealed to residents of the state to support President Bola Tinubu’s administration, saying the federal government’s economic reforms are beginning to show in development and better governance. Okpebholo appealed on Wednesday when he visited the Ojuromi of Uromi, HRH Zaiki Anselm Aidenojie II, at the traditional ruler’s palace in Esan Northeast Local Government Area. He was accompanied by members of the All Progressives Congress (APC), according to a statement by Chief Press Secretary to Okpebholo, Dr. Patrick Ebojele. Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, speaking on Wednesday, October 21, 2026, when he visited the Ojuromi of Uromi, HRH Zaiki Anselm Aidenojie II, at the traditional ruler’s palace, in Esan Northeast Local Government Area. Speaking on his administration’s record, the governor listed road construction, the upgrade of primary healthcare centers, regular payment of salaries, and the building of schools among the areas where work is ongoing. He admitted that much of what his government is doing will not show results overnight. “Most of the work I am undertaking can not manifest in one day. It takes time because it involves construction,” he said. “Many roads have been completed, and we have started several others in different parts of the state. They will ease movement and improve economic activities in Edo,” he said. Governor Okpebholo also spoke about electricity, one of the state’s long-standing challenges. He said a 100-megawatt power plant is expected to come on stream in Edo South in the near future, with another project to add 16 megawatts. “These projects are part of our efforts to address the power problem in the state,” he said. The governor credited the federal government for progress so far. “The man driving that success is Mr. President. That is why I am here to tell you that I do not want Edo to be in opposition to this government because of the progress we are already making,” he said. Earlier, His Royal Highness (HRH) Aidenojie II, Ojuromi of Uromi,speaking on behalf of the Esan Enigies commended the governor for his efforts at fast tracking development to the state. He prayed for God’s blessings and prayed that God would continue to give him wisdom to pilot the affairs of the state. Aidenojie, who described the governor as his son, assured him that the anticipated eight years of his administration would be completed. item.title: How To Protect Yourself From Ebola Infection
item.description: The Federal Government on Tuesday confirmed the first case of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Ebola is a disease that spreads through direct contact with the blood or bodily fluids of an infected person or animal, according to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC). ﻿ Following the confirmation, below are facts on transmission/causes, symptoms, and how to protect yourself and loved ones. How Does It Spread? Ebola can be spread through: Direct contact with blood, sweat, saliva, vomit, or other bodily fluids of an infected, symptomatic person Touching contaminated surfaces such as clothing, bedding, or other materials contaminated with fluids from an infected individual Consuming infected wild animals, handling deceased bodies without safety gear. Know The Symptoms Symptoms typically appear two to 21 days after exposure. The symptoms include: Fever Vomitting Headache Diarrhea Weakness/Fatigue Bleeding Muscle pain Sore throat How To Protect Yourself Wash hands regularly with clean running water and soap, or use alcohol-based sanitiser. Avoid contact with dead bodies and wild animals. Ensure all meat products are handled hygienically and thoroughly cooked. Do not touch bodily fluids of sick individuals or handle deceased bodies without professional health protocols. Health workers should adhere strictly to Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) standards. Myth Vs Facts Let’s set the record straight! Myth: Ebola spreads via casual contact (handshake, hugging). Fact: Ebola does not spread through casual contact. It requires direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person. Myth: Ebola spreads through food and water. Fact: Ebola does not spread through food and water, but all foods should be thoroughly cooked. Drink clean water always. Myth: Ebola spreads through the air. Fact: Ebola is not an airborne virus. Transmission strictly requires direct physical contact with bodily fluids or contaminated objects from a person showing active symptoms. Myth: Healthcare facilities are not safe during outbreaks. Fact: Healthcare facilities are strengthening infection prevention and control measures, including triage systems, hand hygiene, use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), and isolation procedures to protect patients and healthcare workers. Stay informed and avoid panic. Spreading unverified rumours causes unnecessary fear and hampers response efforts. Always rely on official health updates.
